Inspector selects a work date; useDailyReport fetches or lazily creates a daily_reports row (status='draft'). buildDailyReportSnapshot groups annotations by pay_item_id, applies unit conversion, and joins prior_cumulative from v_approved_pay_item_quantities. The result is returned as SnapshotItem[] and displayed as a live preview without persisting.

On submit: (1) buildDailyReportSnapshot is called fresh to produce the frozen snapshot; (2) if no row exists it is inserted as draft+snapshot then immediately updated to submitted; (3) if a rejected/submitted row already exists it is first reset to draft+snapshot, then flipped to submitted; (4) a single update sets status='submitted'. The frozen snapshot JSONB is the source of truth for RE review.

After submit, previewQuery continues running. isStale compares frozen snapshot vs live preview: length mismatch or any per-item delta_quantity diff > 0.005 triggers stale=true. Inspector sees an 'out of date' alert with a Resubmit button, which calls submit() again and replaces the snapshot atomically.

RE calls useApproveReport(reportId) which issues update({status:'approved'}) on daily_reports. Approved rows are excluded from the submitted queue and their snapshot.delta_quantity values become visible through v_approved_pay_item_quantities to downstream quantity-to-payment rollups. useBulkApproveReports handles multiple IDs in a single .in() update.

RE opens ReRejectDialog which enforces a non-empty reason before calling useRejectReport. The mutation: (1) updates daily_reports with status='rejected' and reject_reason; (2) auto-inserts a daily_report_comments row with body='Rejected: <reason>' attributed to the RE user. The inspector sees the rejection reason on their DailyReport page.
Inspector calls reopen() on a rejected report. Mutation issues update({status:'draft'}) only. Inspector can then edit annotations and resubmit.

useReportArchives queries the daily_report_snapshots table (cast as `any` due to missing generated types) and returns historical snapshots with archived_at, archived_reason, and reject_reason. The RE review card renders a diff column comparing current snapshot to prior archive entries.

The daily_reports_status_side_effects DB function is referenced in the stream spec as the notification seam but is NOT present in any migration file found in supabase/migrations/. The send-push edge function exists and accepts {user_id, title, body} with service-role auth, dispatching FCM push via device_tokens table. However, no wiring between daily_report status changes and send-push calls exists in the current codebase.

Four-state FSM: draft → submitted (inspector submit) → approved (RE approve) or rejected (RE reject) → draft (inspector reopen). Approved is a terminal state from the inspector's perspective; no reopen path exists for approved reports.
Consolidated open-risk debt items for daily report lifecycle
gaps: daily_report_snapshots missing from generated types — archive panel silently broken if table absent.
No server-side RLS on approve/reject — any authenticated user can approve reports.
rejected_at / rejected_by not cleared on reopen; approved_by / approved_at not set on approve; rejected_by / rejected_at not set on reject.

leaves.intent: Documents page — three-pane layout: Three-pane layout: folder tree (left), breadcrumb + document list (centre), no persistent right drawer. Folder tree renders system folders sorted before user-created folders; chevron toggle expands nested children. Selecting a folder loads its non-deleted head documents. Breadcrumb reflects the full path from project root.
gaps: Folder drag-and-drop is absent; moveFolder mutation exists in useFolders (line 96) but no drag-source or drop-target UI is wired — folder reorganisation requires direct DB access.
Tree auto-expansion opens ancestors of the auto-selected 'plans' folder (line 148-153) but does not persist expanded state in localStorage — every page reload collapses the tree.

buildTree does not sort user-created child folders independently by name; they are sorted by the same comparator as top-level folders, so a user folder inserted between two system folders can appear out-of-order if its name sorts earlier than a sibling system folder name.

leaves.intent: Folder tree — recursive render, counts, create/rename/delete: Folder tree correctly renders nested hierarchy from parent_id. System folders sort before user folders alphabetically. Folder file counts reflect only non-deleted, non-superseded (head) documents. PM/admin can create, rename, delete (empty) folders; inspectors cannot.
gaps: folderCountsQuery fetches the entire project documents table (all columns) to compute counts — a SELECT * equivalent. A COUNT(*) group-by query would be significantly lighter for projects with large document sets.

deleteFolder on the client calls supabase.from('document_folders').delete() without a prior empty-check in the hook — the server-side block-nonempty trigger (trg_document_folders_block_nonempty) prevents the delete, but the client receives a PostgreSQL RAISE EXCEPTION error message, which is surfaced as a destructive toast with the raw SQL message rather than a friendlier UI-level guard.

System folders can be renamed via the same useFolders.renameFolder mutation; no guard in the mutation or RLS prevents a PM from renaming 'Plans' to an arbitrary name, breaking the system_kind visual hint in KIND_HINTS.

leaves.intent: 10 standard seeded folders auto-created on project insert: Every new project automatically receives 10 system folders: Plans, Specs, RFIs, Submittals, Shop Drawings, Change Orders, Daily Reports, Photos, As-Builts, Correspondence. Existing projects are backfilled. seed_project_standard_folders is idempotent (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING).
gaps: The backfill block also inserts legacy PDF rows into plans/specs folders — if projects.pdf_storage_path or specs_storage_path references a blob that was already deleted from storage, the inserted document row becomes a dangling reference with no storage object.

ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING relies on the partial unique indexes uq_document_folders_top_name and uq_document_folders_child_name. The seed inserts all 10 folders at the top level (parent_id=NULL), so the top-level unique index covers them — correct. However if a user manually created a folder named 'Plans' before the migration ran, the conflict suppresses the system-folder insert and that folder remains non-system with no system_kind, breaking role-gating.
No AFTER INSERT trigger on document_folders validates that exactly 10 system folders exist post-seed; drift from the expected set is not detected at runtime.

leaves.intent: File upload with per-file progress queue and same-name versioning: Uploading a file with the same name as an existing document in the same folder automatically creates a new version (version + 1) linked via replaces_document_id. Upload queue shows per-file pending/uploading/done/error status. Completed items auto-clear after 5 s; failures persist until dismissed.
gaps: runUploads in Documents.tsx and uploadFiles in useDocuments.ts are duplicate upload implementations with slightly different error paths — the page-level runUploads propagates per-file error status to the queue UI; the hook-level uploadFiles surfaces a single toast on first error and aborts remaining files. Both code paths can be triggered; only runUploads is used for the main upload drag/drop/button flow, but uploadFiles is exported and could be called inconsistently.

The same-name version check queries deleted_at-filtered documents implicitly (it does not filter .is('deleted_at', null)). A soft-deleted document with the same name is still considered a prior version, so uploading a file whose name matches a trashed document will link a new v2 to a deleted v1 without user awareness.

Folder upload (folderInputRef) reads webkitRelativePath but only the flat file list is passed to runUploads — sub-directory structure inside the uploaded folder is ignored and all files land in the current folder.
No MIME-type validation occurs before upload; any file type can be placed in any folder, including placing executable files in the Specs or Plans folders.

leaves.intent: system_kind enum on document_folders controls role-gated upload: system_kind column is a CHECK-constrained text column accepting 10 values: plans, specs, rfis, submittals, shop_drawings, change_orders, daily_reports, photos, as_builts, correspondence. Inspectors may only upload to photos or daily_reports system folders; managers/admins can upload anywhere.
gaps: system_kind is stored as text not a Postgres enum; the CHECK constraint enforces valid values but the Supabase-generated TypeScript types in integrations/supabase/types.ts may use string rather than the narrower SystemKind union — silent widening if the generated types are not kept in sync with useDocuments.ts.

The inspector upload RLS policy grants INSERT to any authenticated project member when the target folder's system_kind is in ('photos','daily_reports'). It does not restrict UPDATE or DELETE for inspectors — an inspector who can insert can also soft-delete their own uploads only if deleted_by=auth.uid(), but the policy only covers INSERT; no explicit DENY exists for inspectors attempting DELETE on their own rows.

KIND_HINTS is a UI-only constant in Documents.tsx with no server-side backing; if a future system_kind is added to the DB constraint, it will silently display no hint tooltip in the folder tree sidebar.

leaves.intent: block-nonempty-delete trigger prevents deleting non-empty folders: DELETE on document_folders raises an exception if the folder contains any documents (any deleted_at status) or any subfolders. Trigger name: trg_document_folders_block_nonempty. Function: document_folders_block_nonempty_delete.
gaps: The trigger checks documents WHERE folder_id = OLD.id with no deleted_at filter, meaning a folder containing only soft-deleted (trashed) documents cannot be deleted even after the user considers those documents 'gone'. The user must empty trash or hard-delete the trashed documents in the folder before the folder can be removed.

The exception message includes the folder name via OLD.name concatenation. If the folder name contains a percent sign or single quote it could cause unexpected string formatting — though RAISE EXCEPTION with %% quoting is handled by plpgsql, not raw SQL interpolation, so SQL injection is not a risk; the message may appear mangled in edge cases.

No client-side pre-flight check in deleteFolder (useFolders) warns the user before the DB round-trip fails; the error only surfaces after the mutation call returns the raw PostgreSQL exception as a destructive toast.

leaves.intent: Soft-delete to Trash with Undo toast and Empty Trash: Soft-deleting a document sets deleted_at; an Undo toast within the session restores it. 'Empty Trash' permanently removes DB rows and storage blobs. Trash view shows all deleted documents for the project.
gaps: softDeleteWithUndo in Documents.tsx bypasses the deleteDocument mutation in useDocuments.ts (which invalidates trash/folder-count query keys) and directly calls supabase.from('documents').update() — the Undo path similarly calls supabase directly. The hook mutation is therefore only partially used; two delete code paths exist with slightly different query invalidation patterns.

runEmptyTrash collects storage_path values from the in-memory trash array — if the trash query is stale when Empty Trash is triggered, recently trashed files whose trash query hasn't refreshed will have their DB rows deleted but their blobs orphaned.

The Undo toast has no timeout guard beyond the default toast duration (~5 s). If the user undoes after the toast has visually disappeared but before it is fully dismissed, the undo click handler still fires — correct behaviour — but if the page navigates away in that window the undo is silently lost.

leaves.intent: Version history drawer and restore: Version history drawer shows the full chain of replaces_document_id links in descending order. Clicking 'Restore' creates a new head version (source_kind='restore') pointing at the older blob.
gaps: fetchDocumentVersions fetches ALL documents for a project (line 362: .eq('project_id', projectId) with no folder filter) and walks the chain in JS. For large projects this is O(N) rows transferred on every version drawer open.
Circular replaces_document_id chains (possible if DB rows are manipulated outside the app) would cause fetchDocumentVersions to loop infinitely — no cycle detection guard.

restoreVersion inserts a new row pointing to older.storage_path. It does not check whether that storage path still exists in the bucket — a restore of a version whose blob was deleted (e.g., empty-trash then DB rows still exist because only DB delete ran) will succeed at the DB level but produce a broken document entry.

leaves.intent: Inline PDF and image preview modal via signed URL: PDF and image documents open in a signed-URL preview modal without downloading. Non-previewable types trigger browser download. Signed URLs have 1-hour TTL.
gaps: PDF preview uses <iframe src=signedUrl>. Safari on iOS does not support inline PDF rendering in iframes — the PDF triggers a download instead of rendering, silently degrading to the same behaviour as a non-previewable file.

Signed URL TTL is 3600 s. If a user keeps the preview modal open for >1 hour the iframe src silently expires; no refresh mechanism exists. On a page reload the URL is regenerated, but mid-session expiry is not handled.

isPreviewable gates on mime_type starting with 'image/' but HEIC files (common on iOS) have mime_type 'image/heic'; browser cannot render HEIC natively on non-Safari browsers — the preview will display a broken image.

leaves.intent: Multi-select bulk download and bulk soft-delete: Multi-select checkboxes allow select-all and per-row selection. Bulk download opens each file in a new tab staggered by 250 ms. Bulk soft-delete moves all selected to Trash with a single Undo toast.
gaps: bulkDownload uses window.open() per file — browsers with popup blockers will suppress all but the first window.open() call even with the 250 ms stagger, silently failing to download most files in a bulk selection.

selectedIds is cleared when selectedFolderId changes (line 225 effect) but not when filteredDocs changes due to search — a user can search, select results, clear the search, and still have invisible (now off-screen) IDs in selectedIds that get bulk-deleted.
No size cap on bulk download; selecting and downloading thousands of files calls window.open N times with no cap or warning.

leaves.intent: daily_reports status FSM (DB trigger)
gaps: approved_by = auth.uid() inside a trigger assumes the caller is the approving RE. If a server-side function using service-role key ever approves a report programmatically, auth.uid() returns NULL and approved_by is set to NULL silently — no guard exists.

The trigger fires on ANY UPDATE, not just status changes. The IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.status guard avoids false positives, but if a concurrent UPDATE touches only non-status columns while a status change is in flight, the trigger re-executes the IF block unnecessarily.
No audit log is written by this trigger — status transitions are visible only if old row versions are preserved via a separate CDC mechanism (which does not currently exist).

leaves.intent: daily_report_snapshots archive table + side-effects trigger
gaps: Archive only fires on rejected→draft (reopen). A submitted→approved transition does NOT archive the submitted snapshot — if an RE approves a report with incorrect quantities, there is no immutable record of what was approved before any later corrections.
archived_reason is free-text, not a CHECK constraint enum — nothing prevents a programmatic caller from inserting an unrecognised reason value.
reject_reason is stored redundantly in both daily_reports and daily_report_snapshots. If reject_reason is later corrected on the live row without triggering the archive path, the two records diverge.
The RE notification fan-out uses a FOR LOOP with individual INSERTs — for projects with many REs this is N round-trips inside the trigger. A single INSERT … SELECT would be more efficient.

daily_report_snapshots has no FK back to projects — project_id is a denormalised copy. If the project is deleted (CASCADE from daily_reports), orphaned snapshot rows for the project_id remain unless daily_reports CASCADE removes them first.
No snapshot is archived when a draft is deleted — a deleted draft leaves no trace in the audit table.

leaves.intent: useReReviewQueue hook
gaps: useApproveReport approves via .update({ status: 'approved' }) — it does NOT supply reject_reason, which is correct, but it also does not verify the caller is a resident_engineer before sending the request. The DB RLS policy ('RE updates submitted report') enforces this, but a client error surfaces as a generic 403 with no user-facing explanation.

useRejectReport does a client-side trim check on reason but does NOT enforce a minimum length — a single space character passes the trim check on the client (the DB trigger will catch it, but the UX gives no early warning).
No optimistic updates — approving/rejecting shows a loading state but the card stays in the queue until the invalidation round-trip completes.
useReReviewQueue fetches ALL submitted reports at once — no pagination. For a long-running project with many daily submissions this will grow unbounded.

There is no realtime subscription on daily_reports for the RE queue — a second RE could approve a report while the first RE is viewing it, and the first RE's UI won't update until they manually refetch.

daily_report_snapshots table is cast `as any` — the TypeScript type for ReReportArchive.archived_reason is `string | null` but the generated DB type for the column is also nullable; the any cast masks the need for a type assertion on the snapshot field.

leaves.intent: ReReviewCard component
gaps: diffByItem useMemo depends on archivesQ.data and report.snapshot but archivesQ is only enabled when historyOpen=true — the diff column never renders on initial load even if archives exist, because historyOpen starts false. The diff should be computed independently of the history toggle.

Approve/Reject buttons are always rendered even when readOnly=true in the component's Props — the readOnly prop is passed through to ReRejectDialog but does not disable the Approve button, leaving a potential UI inconsistency.
The snapshot table has no sort controls — items are sorted by item_code (ascending, from the DB) and cannot be reordered client-side.
No print / export button on the ReReviewCard itself — export is available at a higher page level only.
The history section uses lazy-loaded archivesQ (enabled on historyOpen) — if a user expands history on multiple cards simultaneously, N parallel queries are fired with no debounce.
Contract-quantity percentage column uses `it.contract_quantity` from the frozen snapshot. If a contract amendment has since changed the contract quantity, the percentage shown may be stale.
No accessibility attributes (aria-label, role) on the approve/reject icon buttons — keyboard-only users cannot identify the actions.

leaves.intent: ReRejectDialog component
gaps: No minimum character count enforced (e.g. 10 chars) — a single character reason ('x') passes. The DB trigger only checks length(trim(reject_reason)) = 0, so single-character reasons persist.
No character counter or max-length cap — very long reasons are accepted without UX warning.
The textarea placeholder is generic ('Enter reason for rejection…') — no guidance on what constitutes a valid reject reason for compliance purposes (e.g. 'quantity discrepancy', 'missing pay item').
No audit of WHO triggered the rejection beyond rejected_by=auth.uid() in the DB trigger — the reason text is the only human-readable record.

leaves.intent: useDailyReport hook — submit / reopen / isStale
gaps: submit() performs a multi-step mutation (build snapshot → upsert draft → set submitted) without a DB transaction. If the second UPDATE (status flip) fails after the snapshot is already written, the report row is in an inconsistent state (snapshot updated, status still draft).

reopen() flips to draft via a direct UPDATE — the side-effects trigger (which archives the snapshot) fires in the DB, but the client does not wait for or handle archive failures. If the trigger fails (e.g. constraint violation), the row is in draft but no archive was created.

isStale is computed on every render via a side-effect-free useMemo equivalent — but it reads previewQuery.data which is re-fetched every time the query key changes (including on status change). This can cause a brief isStale=true flash after approval even though the report is now approved and the guard `query.data?.status !== 'approved'` should suppress it — the guard disables the previewQuery but previewQuery.data may retain stale data from the last successful fetch.
No optimistic UI on submit — the inspector sees a loading state while the DB round-trip completes.
buildDailyReportSnapshot is called twice on resubmission (once to reset to draft with new snapshot, once to submit) — this doubles the Supabase query load.

leaves.intent: v_approved_pay_item_quantities view
gaps: No RLS policy directly on the view — access is controlled entirely by the underlying daily_reports table's SELECT policies. If a user gains SELECT on daily_reports outside of RLS (e.g. via service-role), they see all approved quantities without project-membership enforcement.

new_cumulative in the view is the cumulative as-of the report's snapshot freeze date. If a report is retroactively corrected (status flipped back to draft and resubmitted), the view returns both the old approved row (from before retraction — which no longer exists because status is now draft/submitted) and the new one. In practice retraction is not possible in the current FSM (approved is terminal) but should be documented as a constraint.
The view is not materialised — every query re-parses all approved snapshots. For projects with hundreds of daily reports this is O(n×items) on every dashboard load.

delta_quantity and new_cumulative are cast from jsonb text with no bounds check — malformed snapshot entries (non-numeric strings) will cause the cast to fail and surface as a query error rather than a NULL.
